title: Same-Name Replacement Pod, forced-deletion fix (root-cause-corrected live replication of F1.1)

p_binding.description: Reusable name still resolves to the decision-time UID.

p_target_resolves.description: Queued name resolves to a concrete resource at actuation.

transitions.title: Attacker force-deletes and recreates the Pod under the same name
transitions.notes: Real transition duration is measured live, not simulated; recorded per trial.

provenance.platform_basis: The Pod object is a byte-identical copy of the locked E13 manifest f1_1_pod_benign.yaml (nodeName: flashir-nonexistent, image registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10.1) -- the exact same never-scheduled Pod design used by the original F1.1 mechanism. E29 diagnosed the original 39-80s deletion latency to Kubernetes' default pod termination grace period, not scheduling or image-pull (neither ever occurs for this Pod). This experiment tests the actual Pod mechanism, not a ConfigMap surrogate, with only the deletion call changed to force immediate removal.
provenance.incident_basis: Autonomous response queues quarantine after confirmed compromise, identical to F1.1.
provenance.policy_basis: Historical compromise still applies to the original object; response must remain bound to the original UID.
provenance.limitations: This experiment tests the identity-rebinding decision mechanism on the same deliberately-unscheduled diagnostic Pod design as the locked F1.1 scenario; it does not itself demonstrate quarantining a real running/scheduled workload, since neither the original F1.1 nor this fixed variant ever schedules the Pod onto a real node.

notes: E32: full live decision trial (not just timing) on the grace-period-fixed real Pod mechanism, combining E29's root-cause diagnosis with E13's original live decision-gate methodology. Tests whether F1.1's actual Pod-based mechanism -- not a ConfigMap substitute -- produces correct decisions within its original 5s deadline once the deletion call is fixed.
